p.src: That day, Song Jiang assigned the parties going to see the lanterns in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness: “Chai Jin and I will go together; Shi Jin with Mu Hong; Lu Zhishen with Wu Song; and Zhu Tong with Liu Tang. Only these four parties shall go; everyone else is to remain here and guard the stronghold.” Li Kui promptly said, “They say the lanterns in the Eastern Capital are splendid. I want to go and see them too.” Song Jiang said, “How could you possibly go?” Li Kui stubbornly insisted on going, and there was no restraining him. Song Jiang said, “Since you insist on going, you are not to cause any trouble. Dress as an attendant and follow me.” He also told Yan Qing to make the journey, specifically to keep Li Kui company.

p.src: Now, dear reader, Song Jiang was a branded man; how could he go to the imperial capital? It turned out that after the divine physician An Daoquan came to the mountain, he applied a poisonous medicine that removed the tattoo, then treated the place with fine remedies, leaving only a red scar. He then obtained fine gold and flawless jade, ground them into a powder, and applied it every day until the scar naturally faded away. The medical books say, “Fine jade removes blemishes,” and this is precisely what they mean.

After them, Song Jiang, Zhu Tong, and Liu Tang also left disguised as merchants. Each wore a saber at his waist and carried a broad-bladed polearm, with concealed weapons hidden about him—needless to say.

p.src: As for Song Jiang and Chai Jin, they disguised themselves as idle minor officials. Dai Zong was told to pose as their clerk and accompany them, so that if any emergency arose, he could fly back with the news. Li Kui and Yan Qing dressed as attendants and each shouldered baggage. When they descended the mountain, all the chieftains escorted them to Golden Sands Strand and gave them a farewell feast. The strategist Wu Yong repeatedly warned Li Kui: “Whenever you go down the mountain, you invariably make trouble. This time you are going with our elder brother to see the lanterns in the Eastern Capital, and it is no ordinary outing. Do not drink wine on the road; be exceedingly cautious and attentive, and do not behave as you usually do. If there is any collision, the brothers will be ashamed to face one another, and we may never be able to gather together again.” Li Kui said, “There is no need for the strategist to worry. I will cause no trouble at all on this journey.”

p.src: After taking their leave, they set out on the road, passed Jizhou, traveled through Tengzhou, proceeded by way of Shanzhou, and came up through Caozhou. At last they saw the Wanshou Gate of the Eastern Capital ahead and found an inn outside it where they lodged. Song Jiang consulted with Chai Jin. This took place on the eleventh day of the first month. Song Jiang said, “I certainly dare not enter the city by daylight tomorrow. We must wait until the night of the fourteenth day of the first month, when crowds fill the streets and all is clamor; only then can we enter.” Chai Jin said, “Tomorrow I will first enter the city with Yan Qing and scout the way.” Song Jiang said, “Excellent.” The next day, Chai Jin put on a neat and proper suit of clothes, with a fresh headscarf and spotless shoes and stockings. Yan Qing’s attire was more elegant still. The two left the inn and observed the households outside the city: every home bustled, every doorway rang with noise. All were preparing to celebrate the Lantern Festival, arranging scenes that proclaimed the blessings of peace. When they reached the city gate, no one stopped them. The Eastern Capital was indeed a magnificent place. How magnificent was it? Behold:

p.src: Its prefecture is named for the Bian River, and its seat is called Kaifeng. Winding onward, it commands the lands of Wu and Chu; stretching afar, it joins the borders of Qi and Lu. Its mountains and rivers form a commanding terrain; it is a vital crossroads by both land and water. Yu assigned it to Yuzhou; under the Zhou it was enfeoffed as the land of Zheng. Its layered contours, like a reclining ox, accord with the central region of Earth in the heavens above; its towering heights, like a crouching tiger, mirror the twenty-eight lunar lodges that gird the sky. On Jinming Pool, willows grace all three months of spring; beside the imperial garden walls, flowers bloom through all four seasons. For a hundred thousand li around, it is a realm where fish and dragons transform; it is the hub where four hundred military prefectures converge like spokes. Dense auspicious clouds enfold the vermilion pavilions; warm and radiant omens shine upon towers and terraces.

p.src: Chai Jin and Yan Qing now entered the city and strolled along the Imperial Avenue, looking about them. Turning beyond the Donghua Gate, they saw streams of people in brocade robes and flowered caps, a dense and bustling crowd distinguished by their various uniforms, all seated in teahouses and taverns. Chai Jin led Yan Qing straight up a small tavern and took a private room overlooking the street. Leaning on the railing, he saw many members of the imperial guard entering and leaving the palace, each wearing a flower of emerald leaves by his temple. Chai Jin called Yan Qing over and whispered in his ear, explaining what he was to do. Yan Qing was quick to understand at the slightest hint. Without asking for details, he hurried downstairs. As he stepped out of the tavern, he happened to meet a sober-looking officer of the imperial guard and bowed in greeting. The man said, “Your face is unfamiliar. I do not believe we have ever met.” Yan Qing said, “My master is an old friend of yours, Inspector, and has specially sent me to invite you.” In fact, the guard’s surname was Wang, but Yan Qing said, “Surely you are Inspector Zhang?” The man said, “My surname is Wang.” Yan Qing instantly replied, “Of course—it was Inspector Wang whom I was told to invite. In my haste and confusion, I forgot.” Inspector Wang followed Yan Qing upstairs. Yan Qing raised the curtain and said to Chai Jin, “I have brought Inspector Wang.” Yan Qing took the insignia from his hand, while Chai Jin invited him into the private room. They exchanged formal greetings. The guardsman Wang studied Chai Jin for a long while but did not recognize him. He said, “My eyes fail me, and I have forgotten you, sir. Since you have been kind enough to summon me, may I ask your honored name?” Chai Jin smiled and said, “You and I were friends in childhood. I shall not tell you just yet, elder brother; think carefully.” Meanwhile, he ordered wine and meat and drank sociably with the inspector. The waiter laid out savory dishes and fruit. Yan Qing poured the wine and pressed it courteously upon their guest. When they were half drunk, Chai Jin asked, “Inspector, what is the meaning of that emerald flower on your head?” The guardsman Wang said, “His present Majesty is celebrating the Lantern Festival. The twenty-four companies serving within and without the palace, on the left and right, number some five thousand seven or eight hundred men in all. Each man has been granted a padded robe and a spray of golden flowers with emerald leaves. On it is a small gold plaque engraved with the four characters ‘Rejoicing Together with the People.’ For that reason, we wait here each day to be inspected and mustered. Anyone who has the palace flower and brocade robe can gain entry to the inner palace.” Chai Jin said, “I had no idea.” After several more cups, Chai Jin said to Yan Qing, “Go and warm me a cup of wine to drink.” Before long the wine arrived. Chai Jin rose and offered the cup to the guardsman Wang, saying, “Drink this cup that I offer you, sir, and only then shall I reveal my name.” The guardsman Wang said, “I truly cannot recall you. I beg you to tell me your honored name.” The guardsman Wang raised the wine and drained it in one draught. No sooner had he swallowed it than saliva ran from the corners of his mouth, his feet flew up, and he collapsed upon the bench. Chai Jin hurriedly removed his own headscarf, clothes, boots, and stockings. He then stripped off the guardsman Wang’s brocade robe, leggings, shoes, trousers, and other garments and put them all on from head to foot. Donning the flowered cap and taking up the insignia, he instructed Yan Qing: “If the waiter comes to ask, merely tell him that this inspector is drunk and the other gentleman has not yet returned.” Yan Qing said, “There is no need to instruct me. I know how to put him off.”

p.src: Auspicious clouds enfold the Phoenix Gate; felicitous mists veil the Dragon Tower. Glazed tiles are laid in paired-mandarin-duck patterns; kingfisher-green curtains hang in tortoiseshell designs. The Zhengyang Gate leads straight onto the imperial way; in the Changchao Hall the sovereign sits in majesty within the Purple Precinct. On the armillary-sphere terrace the stars are observed and calculated; in the court of awaiting dawn, civil and military officials stand in separate ranks. The walls are coated with peppered plaster, while slender green willows brush the soaring eaves; Balustrades encircle the halls, and clusters of purple blossoms greet the imperial litter. One might imagine oneself upon the isle of Penglai, or fancy one's spirit wandering through Tushita Heaven.

He reached the Zichen Hall and passed around the Wende Hall, but every door was secured with a golden lock, so he could not enter. He therefore went around Ninghui Hall, slipped in along its side, and came to a side chamber bearing the three characters “Ruisi Hall” in gold. This was where the Emperor read. A small vermilion door stood open at the side. Chai Jin slipped inside and saw the imperial throne set directly ahead. p.src: When Chai Jin saw the names of the four great outlaws, he thought to himself, “We have so grievously troubled the realm that the Emperor keeps us constantly in mind and has written our names here.” He drew a concealed blade from his person and cut away the four characters “Song Jiang of Shandong.” He hurried out of the hall, and scarcely had he left when someone came along. Chai Jin left the inner gardens, passed out through Donghua Gate, and returned to the winehouse. The palace guardsman Wang was still asleep, so Chai Jin left the brocade robe, flowered cap, and the rest of the uniform in the private room as before. Chai Jin changed back into his former clothes, called Yan Qing, settled the wine bill with the waiter, and gave him the remaining dozen-odd strings of cash as a reward. As he was about to go downstairs, he instructed him, “Inspector Wang and I are sworn brothers. He became drunk just now, so I went into the palace and answered the roll in his place. I have returned, but he is still asleep. I live outside the city and fear the gates may close before I get home. I give you all the money left over; his uniform and livery are here.” “Set your mind at ease, sir,” said the waiter. “I shall attend to him myself.” Chai Jin and Yan Qing left the winehouse and went straight out through Wanshou Gate. When the palace guardsman Wang arose that evening, he found his uniform and flowered cap intact but could not understand what had happened. The waiter repeated Chai Jin's words. Still dazed and stupefied as though drunk, Wang returned home. The next day someone came and said, “The four characters ‘Song Jiang of Shandong’ have disappeared from Ruisi Hall. Today every gate is guarded as tightly as an iron barrel, and everyone entering or leaving is being rigorously questioned.” Wang knew perfectly well what had happened, but how could he dare speak of it?

p.src: To resume: Chai Jin returned to the inn and gave Song Jiang a full account of the inner palace. He took out the four imperial characters naming the great outlaw, “Song Jiang of Shandong,” and showed them to him. Song Jiang sighed without end after seeing them. At dusk on the fourteenth, the bright moon rose in the east and not a wisp of cloud veiled the sky. Song Jiang and Chai Jin dressed as minor officials out for an evening's leisure, Dai Zong as a clerk, and Yan Qing as a young attendant, leaving only Li Kui to watch their rooms. The four mingled with the festival processions and surged in through Fengqiu Gate. They toured all six avenues and three markets; indeed, the night was warm and the breeze gentle, perfect for merrymaking. When they turned into Horse Market Street, every household had erected a lantern awning before its door, competing in the display of lights until all shone as brightly as day. Truly, above and below the towers, fire shone upon fire; amid passing carriages and horses, people gazed upon people. The four turned onto Imperial Street, where “Mist and Moon” signs lined both sides. Midway along they saw a house with a blue-cloth awning outside, mottled-bamboo blinds within, and windows of green gauze on either side. Two signboards hung outside, each bearing five characters: “A goddess among women of song and dance; the foremost beauty of moonlit revels.” On seeing it, Song Jiang entered a teahouse for tea and asked the tea waiter, “Whose is that celebrated courtesan's house ahead?” “She is the foremost courtesan of the upper houses here in the Eastern Capital,” replied the waiter. “Her name is Li Shishi.” “Can she be the one who is so intimate with the present Emperor?” asked Song Jiang. “Do not speak so loudly,” the waiter cautioned. “There are ears and eyes close at hand.” Song Jiang called Yan Qing over and whispered in his ear, “I wish to meet Li Shishi and secretly accomplish our purpose. Devise some tactful means of getting inside. I shall wait here drinking tea.” Song Jiang remained in the teahouse drinking tea with Chai Jin and Dai Zong.

p.src: Yan Qing went straight to Li Shishi's door, raised the blue-cloth awning, lifted the mottled-bamboo blind, and passed through the middle doorway. There hung a paired-mandarin-duck lantern. Beneath it, on a fragrant table lacquered like rhinoceros hide, stood an antique bronze boshan incense burner, from which delicate threads of fragrance curled. Four celebrated landscape paintings hung on the two walls, with four straight-backed chairs lacquered like rhinoceros hide arranged below. Seeing no one emerge, Yan Qing passed through the inner courtyard and came to another large reception room. In it stood three exquisitely carved little beds of fragrant nanmu wood, spread with purple brocade mattresses patterned with falling flowers and flowing water. A splendid array of lanterns hung from a jade frame, and curious antiques were displayed about the room. Yan Qing coughed softly. A maidservant came from behind the screen, curtsied to him, and asked, “What is your honored surname, young master? Where have you come from?” “May I trouble you, elder sister, to ask the madam to come out?” said Yan Qing. “I have something to tell her.” The maid went inside, and before long Madam Li came out. Yan Qing invited her to sit and made four full prostrations. “What is your surname, young man?” asked Madam Li. Yan Qing replied, “Have you forgotten me, madam? I am Zhang Yi's son, Zhang Xian. I have been away since childhood and only returned today.” Now Zhang, Li, and Wang are the commonest surnames in the world. The old bawd pondered for a long while, and the lamplight made faces difficult to distinguish. Suddenly she remembered and cried, “Are you not young Zhang Xian from beneath Taiping Bridge? Where have you been, that you have not come for so long?” “I have long been away from home,” replied Yan Qing, “and so could not come to pay my respects. I now serve a gentleman from Shandong whose wealth is beyond all telling. He is the foremost wealthy gentleman in all Yannan and Hebei. He has come here, first, to enjoy the Lantern Festival; second, to visit relatives in the capital; third, to trade his goods here; and fourth, to seek a single meeting with your young lady. He would not presume to speak of coming and going freely in this house; he asks only to share one drink at the same table, and then his heart's desire will be fulfilled. I do not say this to boast, but the man truly has thousands upon thousands of taels in gold and silver and wishes to present some to this household.” The old bawd was greedy by nature and loved nothing so much as gold and wealth. Hearing Yan Qing's speech, she conceived an interest at once and hurriedly called Li Shishi out to meet him. Seen beneath the lamplight, she was truly beautiful. The moment Yan Qing saw her, he bowed his head to the floor. A poem bears witness:

u.src: Seeing no one emerge, Yan Qing passed through the inner courtyard and came to another large reception room. In it stood three exquisitely carved little beds of fragrant nanmu wood, spread with purple brocade mattresses patterned with falling flowers and flowing water. A splendid array of lanterns hung from a jade frame, and curious antiques were displayed about the room.
Yan Qing coughed softly. A maidservant came from behind the screen, curtsied to him, and asked, “What is your honored surname, young master?
Where have you come from?”
“May I trouble you, elder sister, to ask the madam to come out?” said Yan Qing. “I have something to tell her.”
The maid went inside, and before long Madam Li came out. Yan Qing invited her to sit and made four full prostrations.
“What is your surname, young man?” asked Madam Li.
Yan Qing replied, “Have you forgotten me, madam? I am Zhang Yi's son, Zhang Xian. I have been away since childhood and only returned today.”

Now Zhang, Li, and Wang are the commonest surnames in the world. The old bawd pondered for a long while, and the lamplight made faces difficult to distinguish. Suddenly she remembered and cried, “Are you not young Zhang Xian from beneath Taiping Bridge?
Where have you been, that you have not come for so long?”
“I have long been away from home,” replied Yan Qing, “and so could not come to pay my respects.
I now serve a gentleman from Shandong whose wealth is beyond all telling.

He is the foremost wealthy gentleman in all Yannan and Hebei. He has come here, first, to enjoy the Lantern Festival; second, to visit relatives in the capital; third, to trade his goods here; and fourth, to seek a single meeting with your young lady.
He would not presume to speak of coming and going freely in this house; he asks only to share one drink at the same table, and then his heart's desire will be fulfilled.

u.src: I do not say this to boast, but the man truly has thousands upon thousands of taels in gold and silver and wishes to present some to this household.”
The old bawd was greedy by nature and loved nothing so much as gold and wealth. Hearing Yan Qing's speech, she conceived an interest at once and hurriedly called Li Shishi out to meet him.
Seen beneath the lamplight, she was truly beautiful.
The moment Yan Qing saw her, he bowed his head to the floor.
A poem bears witness:

p.src: In the flower of youth, her fame surpassed the pleasure quarters; her jade features and blossom face had scarcely an equal. All envied her for having lain close beside the sovereign; no shame that even a valiant hero should bow his head before her.

p.src: The procuress told her the whole story, and Li Shishi asked, “Where is the gentleman now?” Yan Qing replied, “He is just across the way, in the teahouse opposite.” Li Shishi said, “Invite him over to my humble home for tea.” Yan Qing said, “Without your word, my lady, he would not presume to enter.” The procuress said, “Hurry and invite him in.” Yan Qing went straight to the teahouse and whispered the news in their ears. Dai Zong took out some money and paid the tea waiter; then the three men followed Yan Qing directly to Li Shishi’s house. They entered the middle gate, where she received them and invited them into the main guest chamber. Li Shishi folded her hands, stepped forward, and courteously inquired after their health, saying, “Master Zhang spoke highly of your distinction a short while ago. Now that you have deigned to visit me, my humble chamber shines with honor.” Song Jiang replied, “I am a rustic from a remote mountain village, narrow in experience and scant in learning. To behold your flower-like countenance is the greatest good fortune of my life.” Li Shishi invited them to sit, then looked at Chai Jin and asked, “And who is this gentleman to you?” Song Jiang said, “This is my cousin, Inspector Ye.” He then had Dai Zong pay his respects to Li Shishi. Song Jiang and Chai Jin sat on the left in the guests’ seats, while Li Shishi accompanied them from the host’s place on the right. When the nurse brought in tea, Li Shishi personally exchanged cups with Song Jiang, Chai Jin, Dai Zong, and Yan Qing. There is no need to describe the fragrance and flavor of that tea. When they had finished their tea and the cups and saucers had been cleared away, they were about to explain their circumstances when the nurse came to report, “His Majesty has arrived at the rear entrance.” Li Shishi said, “I truly dare not ask you to stay. Tomorrow His Majesty will visit the Shangqing Palace and certainly will not come here, so I beg you all to return then, and we shall converse over a few cups of wine.” Song Jiang repeatedly murmured his assent and departed with the other three. After leaving Li Shishi’s gate, they passed through the Little Imperial Street and went straight toward Tianhan Bridge to see the mountain of lanterns. As they passed before Fan Tower, they heard reed pipes and mouth organs shrilling from above, while drums and music thundered to the heavens; the dazzling lanterns held every gaze, and sightseers swarmed like ants. Song Jiang and Chai Jin also went up Fan Tower, found a private room, sat down, and ordered wine and dishes, drinking as they admired the lanterns from above. p.src: Hearing this, Song Jiang hurried over to look. It was “Nine-Dragoned” Shi Jin and “Unrestrained” Mu Hong, both dead drunk in the private room and recklessly spouting wild words. Song Jiang strode up and shouted, “You two brothers nearly frightened me to death! Pay your wine bill at once and get out of here! You are fortunate that I happened upon you; had an officer of the law heard this, no small calamity would have befallen us. Who would have thought that you two brothers could be so ignorant and reckless! Leave the city quickly, without delay. Tomorrow, once we have seen the main lantern display, we shall return that very night. That will be quite enough—do not ruin the whole affair!” Shi Jin and Mu Hong said nothing. They called the wine waiter over and settled their bill. The two went downstairs and made their way out of the city ahead of the others. Song Jiang, Chai Jin, and the other two drank three cups lightly, adding a little color to the spring evening. Dai Zong reckoned up and paid the wine bill, and the four swept their sleeves and descended the tower. They went straight to their inn by the Wanshou Gate and knocked at the door. Li Kui opened his sleepy eyes and said to Song Jiang, “Brother, if you did not mean to take me along, you should have left me behind. But since you brought me, making me guard the room has bored me out of my wits. You have all gone off to enjoy yourselves!” Song Jiang said, “Your temper is unruly and your face is fearsome. It is not that I begrudge taking you into the city; I only fear that you might cause trouble.” Li Kui replied, “If you will not take me, then do not take me. Why make so many excuses? When have you ever seen me frighten anyone’s children or grown folk to death?” Song Jiang said, “I shall take you in for tomorrow night only, the fifteenth. Once we have seen the main lantern display, we shall return that very night.” Li Kui burst into hearty laughter.

u.src: The night passed, and the next day was the Lantern Festival itself. The sky was wonderfully clear and bright.
As evening approached, countless people came out to celebrate the Lantern Festival. The ancients composed a lyric to the tune “Crimson Capital Spring” describing precisely this festival scene:

p.src: The first mild warmth is heralded; auspicious mists suddenly clear, and spring comes early to the starry capital. Kingfisher-green carriages race in flight, jade bridles vie at the gallop; all say the lantern mountain has been decked in color like Penglai’s isle. Toward evening, twin dragons hold lights in their mouths. From atop the Crimson Sky Tower, beneath the vermilion fungus-shaped canopy, all gaze upward upon the imperial presence. Faintly the wind bears the imperial music; in celebration, the Jade Hall shares the spectacle, and all the immortals arrive together. All along the way, imperial incense fills the air, and the mortal world opens into laughter and delight. A tiny star-ball gleams; gradually, faintly, the cracking of whips dies away into silence. The revelers return beneath the moon, while the enchanted realm has yet to see dawn.

p.src: That night, Song Jiang and Chai Jin again disguised themselves as idle officials out enjoying the cool air. Taking Dai Zong, Li Kui, and Yan Qing with them, the five went straight in through the Gate of Ten Thousand Years. Although there was no curfew that night, the officers and soldiers at every gate were fully armed. All wore military dress and caps, with bows and crossbows strung and swords drawn, and their deployment was exceedingly strict and orderly. Grand Marshal Gao himself led five thousand armored cavalrymen in patrolling and guarding the city walls. Song Jiang and his four companions jostled and squeezed through the crowd until they were well inside the city. Song Jiang first called Yan Qing over and whispered in his ear, giving him detailed instructions, then said, “We shall wait for one another at the teahouse we visited last night.” Yan Qing went straight to Li Shishi’s house and knocked. Mother Li and the courtesan Li both came out to receive him, saying, “Please ask Master Da not to blame us. His Majesty comes here incognito at unpredictable times, so how could our household dare be careless?” Yan Qing said, “My master repeatedly asked me to convey his respects to Mother Li. We have put the queen of flowers to trouble, yet our remote corner by the Shandong coast has nothing especially rare to offer. Even the few things produced there would not be pleasing if we brought them. He has therefore instructed this humble servant first to present a hundred taels of gold as a token gift. Later, when he finds something truly rare, he will respectfully send that as well.” Mother Li asked, “Where is the master now?” Yan Qing replied, “He is waiting at the mouth of the lane for me to deliver the gift, so that we may go together to see the lanterns.” Of all things in the world, a greedy old bawd loves money best. When she saw Yan Qing take out two pieces of gold glowing like red-hot charcoal and set them before her, how could her heart remain unmoved? She said, “Today is the Lantern Festival, and my daughter and I were just about to share a few cups at a family feast. If the master does not disdain us, perhaps he would consent to visit our humble home and converse awhile.” Yan Qing said, “I shall go and invite him. He is certain to come.” With that, he turned back to the teahouse and related the conversation to Song Jiang, whereupon they all went to Li Shishi’s house. Song Jiang ordered Dai Zong and Li Kui to wait outside the door. The other three entered the main reception hall, where Li Shishi welcomed them and bowed her thanks, saying, “Though this is our first meeting, Master, why have you bestowed so generous a gift upon me? To refuse it would be discourteous, yet to accept it is far more than I deserve.” Song Jiang replied, “Our rustic mountain country has absolutely nothing rare. I have merely sent a trifling token to express my regard. There is no need for the queen of flowers to thank me.” Li Shishi invited them into a small upper chamber, where host and guests took their places. Nurses and maidservants brought forth rare fruits, exquisitely prepared vegetables, unusual delicacies to accompany the wine, and savory dishes, all served in precious vessels until the table was heaped as richly as a spring terrace. Li Shishi took a wine cup, stepped forward, and bowed, saying, “We must have been joined by fate in a former life, for tonight I have met you two gentlemen. With this modest fare, I offer my respects to my honored elders.” Song Jiang said, “Though I possess some hundreds and thousands in idle wealth in my mountain village, I have never witnessed such splendor. The queen of flowers’ fame for beauty and refinement has spread throughout the world. To gain a single audience with you is as difficult as ascending to heaven, much less to receive food and wine from your own hand.” Li Shishi said, “Your praise is far too generous. How could I deserve it?” After they had all exchanged toasts, she ordered the nurse to circulate and pour wine into small golden cups. Whenever Li Shishi spoke of some amusing or elegant matter from the city streets, Chai Jin answered her, while Yan Qing stood to one side, joining in the banter and laughter.

p.src: After several rounds of wine, Song Jiang’s tongue loosened. He bared his arms, brandished his fists, and jabbed his fingers about, revealing the manners of Liangshan Marsh. Chai Jin laughed and said, “My cousin has always been like this after drinking. Please do not laugh at him, my lady.” Li Shishi said, “What harm is there in each person following his own nature?” A maid said, “There are two attendants outside the door. One has a yellow beard and a truly frightening appearance, and he is muttering curses outside.” Song Jiang said, “Call the two of them in.” Presently Dai Zong appeared, leading Li Kui into the chamber. When Li Kui saw Song Jiang and Chai Jin seated drinking with Li Shishi, he was already half consumed with resentment. His strange eyes opened round and wide as he glared straight at the three of them. Li Shishi asked, “Who is this fellow? He looks just like the little demon standing beside the judge in an earth-god temple.” Everyone laughed. Li Kui did not understand what she meant. Song Jiang replied, “He is a servant born in our household, Little Li.” Li Shishi laughed and said, “I myself do not mind, but you have rather insulted Scholar Li Taibai.” Song Jiang said, “This rascal does possess martial skill. He can carry a load of two or three hundred catties and fight thirty or fifty men.” Li Shishi ordered a large silver presentation goblet brought out and gave each man three goblets of wine; Dai Zong also drank three. Fearing that Li Kui might blurt out something improper, Yan Qing gave him a warning look and sent him and Dai Zong back to sit outside the door as before. Song Jiang said, “Why should a true man drink from a little cup?” He took the presentation goblet and drained several in succession. Li Shishi softly sang Su Dongpo’s lyric “The Great River Flows East.” Carried away by the wine, Song Jiang asked for paper and brush. p.src: South of heaven, north of earth—tell me, where beneath the firmament can a wild wanderer find refuge? I have borrowed Shandong’s misty waters and mountain stronghold, and come to purchase the springtime charms of the Phoenix City. Emerald sleeves enfold fragrance; crimson gauze veils snow-white skin—a single smile is worth a thousand in gold. With such an immortal’s grace, how could a faithless rogue be worthy of it? I think of the reed-leaf strand and the islet fringed with smartweed, where the bright moon vainly congeals the waters into jade. Six ranks of six wild geese joined with eight and nine—we wait only for tidings of the golden cock. Our righteous courage embraces heaven, our loyal hearts overshadow earth, yet no one within the four seas knows us; amid ten thousand pangs of parting sorrow, one night in drunkenness turns the hair white.

p.src: When he had finished writing, he handed it to Li Shishi, who read it over and over but could not understand its meaning. Song Jiang was waiting for her to ask for the full particulars, intending then to confide the innermost purpose in his heart, when the nurse came to report, “His Majesty has come through the underground passage and reached the rear gate.” Li Shishi hurriedly said, “I cannot see you farther. I earnestly beg your pardon.” She went straight to the rear gate to receive the imperial visitor. The nurse and maidservants hurriedly cleared away the cups, dishes, and other things, carried off the tables, and swept the pavilion and veranda. Song Jiang and the others had not yet gone out but slipped into a dark corner. Peering from there, they saw Li Shishi kneel before the Emperor, inquire after his health, and express concern that His Majesty had wearied his august person. The Son of Heaven appeared wearing a soft-gauze Tang cap and a dragon-embroidered robe. He said, “Today We visited the Shangqing Temple and have only just returned. We ordered the Crown Prince to distribute imperial wine to the people from the Xuande Tower, and Our imperial brother to purchase goods in the Thousand-Pace Gallery. We had arranged to meet Grand Marshal Yang, but after waiting long and finding that he did not come, We came here alone. Come closer, beloved lady, and converse with Us.” From the darkness Song Jiang said, “If we let this chance pass, another will be hard to find. Why should the three of us not ask him here and now for an edict granting amnesty and accepting our submission?” Chai Jin said, “How could we do that? Even if he agreed now, the decision might later be reversed.” The three were still conferring in the shadows. Now Li Kui had seen Song Jiang and Chai Jin drinking with that beautiful woman while he and Dai Zong were made to guard the door. The hair on his head stood on end, and his belly was full of anger with nowhere to vent it. Just then Grand Marshal Yang lifted the curtain, pushed open the folding door, and strode straight in. Seeing Li Kui, he shouted, “Who are you, fellow? How dare you be here?” Li Kui made no reply. He snatched up a folding chair and struck Grand Marshal Yang squarely in the face. Grand Marshal Yang was taken utterly by surprise and, before he could defend himself, was knocked to the floor with two blows of the chair. Dai Zong came to intervene, but how could he possibly restrain him? Li Kui tore down a painting and set it alight at a candle, thrusting the flame here and there as he started a fire; meanwhile, he smashed the incense table, chairs, and stools to splinters. Hearing the commotion, Song Jiang and the other two rushed out to look and saw the Black Whirlwind, his clothes stripped halfway off, committing mayhem there. The four dragged him outside, but once in the street Li Kui seized a staff and fought his way straight out to the Lesser Imperial Avenue. Seeing that his frenzy had taken hold, Song Jiang had no choice but to hurry out of the city first with Chai Jin and Dai Zong. Fearing that the forbidden gates would close and leave them unable to escape, he left only Yan Qing to keep watch over Li Kui. A fire broke out at Li Shishi’s house, frightening the Emperor Zhao into fleeing like a trail of smoke. The neighbors fought the fire while rescuing Grand Marshal Yang; there is no need to dwell on all that. Cries of slaughter rose throughout the city, shaking heaven and earth. Grand Marshal Gao, who was patrolling the northern gate, heard what had happened and led his troops in pursuit. As Yan Qing accompanied Li Kui in the fighting, they ran into Mu Hong and Shi Jin. All four, armed with spears and staffs, joined forces and fought their way straight to the city’s edge. The gate guards hastened to shut the gate, but outside Lu Zhishen was already whirling his iron monk’s staff, Pilgrim Wu brandished his twin precept blades, and Zhu Tong and Liu Tang gripped their broad-bladed swords. They charged into the city and rescued the four men within. They had only just passed through the city gate when Grand Marshal Gao’s troops arrived outside in pursuit. The eight chieftains could not find Song Jiang, Chai Jin, or Dai Zong, and were growing anxious.

u.src: When he had finished writing, he handed it to Li Shishi, who read it over and over but could not understand its meaning.

Song Jiang was waiting for her to ask for the full particulars, intending then to confide the innermost purpose in his heart, when the nurse came to report, “His Majesty has come through the underground passage and reached the rear gate.”
Li Shishi hurriedly said, “I cannot see you farther. I earnestly beg your pardon.”
She went straight to the rear gate to receive the imperial visitor.
The nurse and maidservants hurriedly cleared away the cups, dishes, and other things, carried off the tables, and swept the pavilion and veranda.

Song Jiang and the others had not yet gone out but slipped into a dark corner. Peering from there, they saw Li Shishi kneel before the Emperor, inquire after his health, and express concern that His Majesty had wearied his august person.

The Son of Heaven appeared wearing a soft-gauze Tang cap and a dragon-embroidered robe. He said, “Today We visited the Shangqing Temple and have only just returned. We ordered the Crown Prince to distribute imperial wine to the people from the Xuande Tower, and Our imperial brother to purchase goods in the Thousand-Pace Gallery.
We had arranged to meet Grand Marshal Yang, but after waiting long and finding that he did not come, We came here alone.
Come closer, beloved lady, and converse with Us.”

From the darkness Song Jiang said, “If we let this chance pass, another will be hard to find. Why should the three of us not ask him here and now for an edict granting amnesty and accepting our submission?”
Chai Jin said, “How could we do that?
Even if he agreed now, the decision might later be reversed.”
The three were still conferring in the shadows.

Now Li Kui had seen Song Jiang and Chai Jin drinking with that beautiful woman while he and Dai Zong were made to guard the door. The hair on his head stood on end, and his belly was full of anger with nowhere to vent it.
Just then Grand Marshal Yang lifted the curtain, pushed open the folding door, and strode straight in. Seeing Li Kui, he shouted, “Who are you, fellow?
How dare you be here?”
Li Kui made no reply. He snatched up a folding chair and struck Grand Marshal Yang squarely in the face.
Grand Marshal Yang was taken utterly by surprise and, before he could defend himself, was knocked to the floor with two blows of the chair.
Dai Zong came to intervene, but how could he possibly restrain him?
Li Kui tore down a painting and set it alight at a candle, thrusting the flame here and there as he started a fire; meanwhile, he smashed the incense table, chairs, and stools to splinters.
Hearing the commotion, Song Jiang and the other two rushed out to look and saw the Black Whirlwind, his clothes stripped halfway off, committing mayhem there.
The four dragged him outside, but once in the street Li Kui seized a staff and fought his way straight out to the Lesser Imperial Avenue.

Seeing that his frenzy had taken hold, Song Jiang had no choice but to hurry out of the city first with Chai Jin and Dai Zong. Fearing that the forbidden gates would close and leave them unable to escape, he left only Yan Qing to keep watch over Li Kui.

p.src: It turned out that the strategist Wu Yong had already foreseen what would happen and had deliberately arranged for a great uproar in the Eastern Capital. Having fixed the exact day and hour, he dispatched five Tiger Generals at the head of a thousand armored cavalrymen. That night they arrived just in time to wait outside the Eastern Capital. There they met Song Jiang, Chai Jin, and Dai Zong; the spare horses they had brought were given to the three to mount, and the rest of the party soon arrived as well. Just as they were all mounting, they discovered that Li Kui was missing from their midst. Grand Marshal Gao’s troops came charging out. Song Jiang’s five Tiger Generals—Guan Sheng, Lin Chong, Qin Ming, Huyan Zhuo, and Dong Ping—dashed to the city wall, reined in their horses beside the moat, and shouted, “All the heroes of Liangshan Marsh are here! Surrender the city at once, and your lives will be spared!” When Grand Marshal Gao heard this, how could he dare come out of the city? In alarm, he ordered the drawbridge raised and all the soldiers onto the walls to guard against attack. Song Jiang summoned Yan Qing and instructed him, “You get along best with that black fellow. Wait here a little for him, then follow us together. I shall return first with the troops and generals, riding through the night to the stronghold, lest some further trouble arise on the road.”

p.src: No more need be said of Song Jiang and the troops departing. Let us instead tell how Yan Qing, watching from beneath the eaves of a house, saw Li Kui fetch his baggage from the inn and take up his twin axes. With a mighty roar, Li Kui leaped through the inn door and set off alone to attack the walled city of the Eastern Capital. Indeed: His roar like giant thunder shook the inn behind; great axes in hand, he went to hew the city gate. How Black Whirlwind Li Kui went about attacking the city will be revealed in the next chapter.
